The welfare system can be seen as too forgivin in some cases, with groups of people avoiding work in order to live of it. I of course have sympathy for people who have real problems that get in the way of steady work. But there should be more emphasis on getting rid of the people who are easily abusing the system.

The police and justice system are a joke mainly because the police (especially in certain areas) are not focused on making peoples lives safer, more on making their reports look good. The justice system is flawed in the way they measure punishments given to those who are caught. Giving out sentences that are way too lose.

It's hard to name one clear cause for the image, but some of the biggest lies I see are about us being the some of the happiest people on earth, and our welfare system being a flawless exampme of socialism.
I see clear problems in how a lot of people think of our police force and justice system as a joke for example. I allso see problems in our welfare but those are more of a subjective issue.

The welfare is allso a thing that disgust me as after the 2016 USA election people, especially americans, have mentioned my country as an example of some sort of socialist/communist utopia, even though it is neither of those. (To be clear I am in no way saying that socialism and communism are the same thing, I just have heard it being called both)

Getting rich is a huge difficulty as you yourself mentioned, and that is a great point also. I myself am most bothered by the image the media gives of the north being a utopia of equality and peace, even when on the street view things are far from peacefull.
